upstream.scope: The installable-R1 package gate (D1 §§15, 18, 19.1, 20, 25–27, 29, 32; D2 T23–T24, T32–T34): a build-from-source package of srtop and the bridge (in the devbox, base images pinned by digest) and the generic macOS client (ad-hoc linker signature, no notarization), user-owned install/update/rollback/uninstall, live checks against the devbox of protocol compatibility, host keys, authentication, reconnect and replacement, a package with no process-changing action that is labelled and keyboard-operable, a repeatable privacy audit, a clean-account walkthrough and a VoiceOver checklist for the user to run, and the R1 notes with the PX-010-G01 support envelope. Test, script and documentation change only: no client, SDK, runtime, protocol, registry, srtop or generated-file change

entries.feature: Reproducible build and install: the devbox Dockerfile pins rust:1-bookworm@sha256:e6f2cff3… (rustc 1.99.1) and debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:734a72b3… (Debian 12.15); srtop and srui-ssh-bridge build --locked from a git archive of the revision, the image labelled with it; the macOS client builds with swift build -c release under the pinned toolchain (Xcode 26.2, Swift 6.2.3, macOS 14 minimum, swift-protobuf 1.38.1 locked) and carries only the linker's ad-hoc signature (Signature=adhoc, flags adhoc,linker-signed); apps/srtop/r1/srui-r1-install.sh installs it under ~/.local/share/srui-r1 with current and previous releases, update, rollback, status and an uninstall that removes only the files it wrote (and, with --purge-settings, only saved-connections.json and its .unreadable backup), refusing root, a prefix outside the home directory and a foreign non-empty directory; the installed release binary connected to the devbox (its bridge started in the box as srui) and was stopped by its PID; selftest.sh covers every refusal, update, retention, rollback and the precise uninstall

Compatible profiles and the client's own refusals against the live devbox srtop (round 2 split): a standard-widgets/1 client reaches the data plane with event dispatch enabled, the wait now including isEventDispatchEnabled (verifier F2: the round-1 wait sampled dispatch before the renderer enabled it; 5 consecutive green runs since); a client requiring a profile the server lacks gets 'Server does not satisfy client required profiles: [...]', a server whose SERVER WELCOME is rewritten to core 1.5.0 gets 'SERVER WELCOME core_version 1.5.0 is not compatible with 0.5.0', both with revision 0, no dispatch and a blocking Connection Failed alert; a mutant accepting any WELCOME core version is killed by this test and by HandshakeNegotiationTests

Unknown and changed host keys and an unauthorized key against the live devbox sshd, through the connection manager with the production known-hosts hint: each ends sshFailedBeforeStream before any SRUI byte with a blocking Connection Failed alert quoting ssh (No ED25519 host key is known … Host key verification failed; Permission denied (publickey)) and saying SRUI never adds or changes host keys, with no trust-anyway path; the known_hosts files are byte-for-byte unchanged; the argv carries StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, BatchMode=yes and UpdateHostKeys=no

Reconnect and server replacement against the live devbox: the box's srui-ssh-bridge killed by its confirmed PID leaves the window subtitled disconnected — showing data from revision N (stale) and the next attempt resumes the same session with RESUME_OK (connecting, ready); srtop stopped by SIGTERM and started again on the same socket gives connecting, replaced, ready, a new session ID, the Session Replaced alert naming it, the subtitle session replaced — rebuilding and a new window built from the new snapshot; devbox.sh drop-bridges and restart-srtop do the same for the manual checklist; round 2 (F7): the file the real client store (SavedConnectionStore) wrote during this test is kept and audited by privacy-audit.sh: host, port, user, label, id, session ID and revision only

The live package offers no process-changing action and is labelled and keyboard-operable: all 41 event-accepting nodes of the T35 snapshot (views, queries, columns, follow, tree, threads, tags) and every native button title are checked against a kill/terminate/signal/renice/priority/affinity/suspend/ptrace/limit pattern; every one has a native accessibility label and role; PX-016's 18 shortcuts are bound with no diagnostic, announced by label and shortcut help, in published reading order; ⌘F, ⌥⌘F, ⌘L, Down (the inspector follows the selected PID over the wire) and ⌘I work against live data

Repeatable privacy and disclosure audit: apps/srtop/r1/privacy-audit.sh scans files or directories for private keys, GitHub/GitLab/AWS/Slack/OpenAI-style tokens, JWTs, bearer credentials, password assignments, URL credentials and private paths, printing only class and location; --self-test plants one secret of each class (built at run time) and passes 21 of 21 cases; live: a worker's --api-token=ghp_… and --password=… arguments are shown on selection and appear in none of srtop's log, the box's sshd output and the client's unified log, which the audit then passes; mutants that drop the token or the private-key rule are killed; round 2 (F8): a /home/<name>/ rule (the devbox's throwaway /home/srui excepted) and a $HOME case planted outside /Users and /home, so each path rule has a case only it can find (22 of 22), and mutants that disable either are killed; the live checks also audit the saved-connections file

The clean-account walkthrough script: refuses root and sudo before writing anything; writes one self-validating result file (STEP lines with exit codes and durations, SUMMARY derived from them, CHECKSUM of every line before it, --verify re-checks both; home as ~, checkout as <checkout>, host as <host>); its sandbox-exec dry run, allowed to write only inside a throwaway HOME, runs install, update, rollback, roll-forward, privacy audit, uninstall and the unrelated-data check against stand-ins and ends DRY-RUN-OK; a failing prerequisite makes its step and the summary FAIL; an edited result fails --verify; mutants that report PASS on a failed command or ignore failures in the summary are killed; round 2 (F3): before any write it refuses (exit 4, the HOME byte for byte unchanged) an account that already has the install prefix, saved-connections.json or its .unreadable backup, ~/.codex/srtop-devbox or a srtop-devbox container; --allow-existing-srui-data overrides, documented as dangerous, and still keeps saved connections it did not create; a failed preflight or prerequisites step stops the run with SUMMARY FAIL before anything is planted, built or installed; round 2 (F4): checklist-session.sh edits ~/.ssh/config only through ssh-config-alias.sh, which refuses a symbolic link, an existing block or srtop-devbox host and restores an absent, empty, unterminated, ordinary or 0600 file byte for byte with its mode; mutants for each are killed

entries.feature: R1 notes: scope, out of scope (htop parity, process actions, privileged helper, external automation, advanced diagnostics, signed or notarized distribution), pinned environments with versions and digests, the PX-010-G01 measurements quoted as recorded on the 27-node shell beside what scale_test.rs enforces today (no timing for 1,000 rows; under 3,000 ms per 10,000-row step; SHELL_NODE_COUNT 82), no bandwidth claim, the compatibility, security and privacy results, the two blocked user items, known gaps and the known follow-ups; round 2: the server-refusal item as blocked on PX-026-G02 using the existing refusal, and the follow-ups PX-024 V3-4, PX-025 worker bounds, PX-068 layout persistence, PX-026 automated selection highlight and the fixed flaky wait

BLOCKED: awaiting PX-026-G02. The server's own refusals of an incompatible client must be clear to the user: a client offering only standard-widgets/2 and a client of core 1.5.0 (its CLIENT HELLO rewritten in flight) must each see 'server refused the handshake: ...' naming the profile or the version, and the connection manager's alert must not say 'transport ended'. The live test exists and fails against today's sessiond (5 of 5 runs: 'transport ended: receive stream closed by peer'); PX-026-G02 makes sessiond send the existing ServerHandshakeRefused{UNSPECIFIED, bounded detail} before closing
